target.title: fix(gateway): don't over-claim a crash on a 1006 abnormal close
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators seeing a WebSocket `1006` (abnormal closure) error from the gateway were told the gateway may have **"crashed or was terminated unexpectedly"** as a co-equal cause. In practice, `1006` most often means a connection was dropped under load (for example, a burst of parallel in-process tool calls or event-loop saturation), not a process crash — so an operator pattern-matching the word "crashed" could restart a healthy production gateway.

This addresses **ask 3 of #100941 only** (the misleading error copy). The architectural asks — connection pooling for in-process tool→gateway calls and a concurrency cap on parallel platform tool fan-out — are intentionally out of scope here.

Refs #100941

## Why This Change Was Made

Reworded the `1006` troubleshooting block in `formatGatewayCloseError` (`src/gateway/call.ts`) so it:

- leads with the actionable, most-common cause — *connection dropped under load, retry*;
- keeps the still-valid causes (gateway not yet ready; TLS mismatch);
- demotes the gateway-crash hypothesis to a rare case the operator should **verify** rather than assume;
- keeps the existing `openclaw doctor` diagnostics call-to-action.

## User Impact

Operators seeing a `1006` now get an accurate, actionable message and are no longer nudged toward restarting a gateway that is almost certainly still healthy. Distinct tool-result retries are already handled by callers; this only changes the human-readable diagnostics.

## Evidence

Regression test in `src/gateway/call.test.ts` ("does not over-claim a gateway crash on a 1006 abnormal close") asserts the new `connection dropped … retry` copy, the absence of the old `crashed or was terminated unexpectedly` over-claim, and that the `openclaw doctor` hint is retained. The gateway test shard is green.
